description: manni docs meta/schemas/encrypted-fields, run in a repo whose schema marks owner x-manni-encrypt, with the key in manni.config.yaml and the page's four pages.

steps.description: Four pages, four states, one run, with the key available.

runShell.stdio: /must be equal to one of the allowed values  \(line 3\)  \[\.\/schemas\/page\.json\][\s\S]*\[encrypted:plain\][\s\S]*\[encrypted:unreadable\][\s\S]*4 files checked, 1 passed, 3 failed, 3 errors/

steps.description: Make a copy of the config without the key.
With no key, the check goes quiet: one warning counts the dropped values, and encrypted:plain still fires.

runShell.stdio: 3 encrypted values were not verified: no encryption key is available.

steps.description: The dropped findings pass; encrypted:plain still fails.
fill encrypts the plain value the page already holds, with no model call.

runShell.command: manni meta fill docs/plain.md --fields owner --dry-run --provider mock

steps.description: A query UPDATE writes the marked property encrypted.

runShell.command: manni meta query "UPDATE docs SET owner = 'platform' WHERE _path = 'docs/auth.md'"

steps.description: Reads do not decrypt: a SELECT returns what the page holds.

runShell.command: manni meta query "SELECT _path, owner FROM docs"

steps.description: What a reviewer sees: the findings ride the github reporter.
A value that decrypts under neither key stops the rotation, and nothing is written.

runShell.stdio: /docs\/wrong-key\.md: \/owner  skipped: does not decrypt under the current key[\s\S]*Key not written: 1 value could not be re-encrypted\./
